ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Repeated disease in the same lobe

A 3-year-old has a third episode of radiographically confirmed pneumonia in the right lower lobe. Between episodes he has persistent localized wheeze. A parent now recalls an abrupt coughing episode while he ate nuts months earlier. Which underlying problem should be investigated?

  1. A retained endobronchial foreign body
  2. Cystic fibrosis
  3. Primary ciliary dyskinesia
  4. Primary antibody deficiency
  5. Recurrent viral-induced wheeze
Answer and explanation

A retained endobronchial foreign body

Recurrent infection in the same region with focal wheeze and choking history suggests localized bronchial obstruction.

Option explanations

A retained endobronchial foreign body: Recurrent infection in the same region with focal wheeze and choking history suggests localized bronchial obstruction.

Cystic fibrosis: This may cause recurrent respiratory infections, but the fixed focal pattern and choking event favor local obstruction.

Primary ciliary dyskinesia: This produces chronic airway disease, often with longstanding upper-airway features, rather than a new focal pattern after choking.

Primary antibody deficiency: Immunodeficiency can cause recurrent infections, but localized disease and a suggestive aspiration event make obstruction more likely.

Recurrent viral-induced wheeze: This typically produces episodic, more diffuse symptoms rather than repeatedly confirmed pneumonia in one lobe after choking.
